extracted.intended_audience: self-regulatory organizations (exchanges), securities lawyers, SEC staff, and market participants who file or review SEC rule filings
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive requirements and steps for exchanges (self-regulatory organizations) to file proposed rule changes with the SEC, and for how the Commission processes, publishes, suspends, institutes proceedings on, or accepts withdrawals of such filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing under Section 19(b)(1) and Rule 19b-4
rubrics_metrics.description: On September 1, 2023, Cboe BYX Exchange, Inc. filed with the Commission, pursuant to Section 19(b)(1) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, and Rule 19b-4 thereunder, a proposed rule change to amend certain connectivity and port fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed rule changes by exchanges must be filed with the Commission pursuant to 15 U.S.C. 78s(b)(1) and the implementing rule 17 CFR 240.19b-4. The filing should identify the rule changes and statutory basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate effectiveness under Section 19(b)(3)(A)
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed rule change was immediately effective upon filing with the Commission pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(A) of the Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A proposed rule change may take effect upon filing with the Commission if it is designated by the exchange as 'establishing or changing a due, fee, or other charge imposed by the self-regulatory organization on any person, whether or not the person is a member of the self-regulatory organization.' (15 U.S.C. 78s(b)(3)(A)(ii)). Filers should designate filings appropriately when they involve fees or charges to seek immediate effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication for public comment in the Federal Register
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed rule change was published for comment in the Federal Register on September 20, 2023.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed rule changes that are filed are published in the Federal Register to solicit public comment; filings should be prepared for publication (including necessary captions, citations) and stakeholders should monitor the Federal Register for published notices and comment periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission authority to temporarily suspend under Section 19(b)(3)(C)
rubrics_metrics.description: On September 29, 2023, pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(C) of the Act, the Commission: (1) temporarily suspended the proposed rule change; and (2) instituted proceedings under Section 19(b)(2)(B) of the Act to determine whether to approve or disapprove the proposed rule change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission may, under 15 U.S.C. 78s(b)(3)(C), temporarily suspend effectiveness of a filing. Filers should be aware that immediate effectiveness can be suspended by the Commission when it deems appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission institution of proceedings under Section 19(b)(2)(B)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission instituted proceedings under Section 19(b)(2)(B) of the Act to determine whether to approve or disapprove the proposed rule change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When proceedings are instituted under 15 U.S.C. 78s(b)(2)(B), the Commission will review the merits of the proposed rule change; filers should be prepared to respond to inquiries and provide supporting information during such proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exchange withdrawal of proposed rule change
rubrics_metrics.description: On October 25, 2023, the Exchange withdrew the proposed rule change (SR-CboeBYX-2023-013).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An exchange may withdraw a previously filed proposed rule change. Filers who intend to withdraw should follow the procedural practice for notifying the Commission and the public, and note the withdrawal in the record (including docket/file number).

rubrics_metrics.name: Document heading and drafting components for Federal Register notices
rubrics_metrics.description: Document headings vary by document type but may contain the following: the agency or agencies that issued and signed a document; the number of the CFR title and the number of each part the document amends, proposes to amend, or is directly related to; the agency docket number / agency internal file number; the RIN which identifies each regulatory action listed in the Unified Agenda.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the Document Drafting Handbook for details on required headings and structure when preparing Federal Register notices. Include required bibliographic metadata (agency, CFR parts, docket numbers, RIN) to ensure correct publication and indexing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of official printed/PDF edition for legal research and legal notice
rubrics_metrics.description: This site displays a prototype of a 'Web 2.0' version of the daily Federal Register. It is not an official legal edition of the Federal Register, and does not replace the official print version or the official electronic version on GPO’s govinfo.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Those relying on FederalRegister.gov for legal research should verify results against an official edition of the Federal Register (printed or the official PDF on govinfo.gov). Until the Administrative Committee of the Federal Register grants official status, the XML rendition on FederalRegister.gov does not provide legal notice to the public or judicial notice to the courts. Only official editions provide legal notice under 44 U.S.C. 1503 & 1507.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citations and footnote referencing to statutory authority
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice cites statutory provisions (e.g., 15 U.S.C. 78s(b)(1), 15 U.S.C. 78s(b)(3)(A), 15 U.S.C. 78s(b)(3)(C), 15 U.S.C. 78s(b)(2)(B)) and implementing regulations (e.g., 17 CFR 240.19b-4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing filings and Federal Register notices, include precise statutory and regulatory citations and explanatory footnotes as appropriate to show the authority and procedural basis for actions taken.
